summary.goals: Amina is preparing for two fixed school mock assessments: Chemistry first, with the outcome of independently solving and explaining amount-of-substance, concentration, balanced-equation and limiting-reagent problems, including unfamiliar numbers and error checks; and Biology three days later, with the outcome of explaining cell transport and enzyme investigations, interpreting unfamiliar data and justifying an independent experimental conclusion. She also wants to preserve both outcomes, keep Friday free and retain the existing English reading submission. She prefers useful explanation and independent application over rereading or arbitrary question counts.
summary.resources: Three uploaded teacher/student documents are available. The Chemistry pack includes worked examples showing division of grams by grams per mole, conversion of millilitres to litres, and comparison of supplied amount divided by coefficient before using the smaller reaction extent. It also contains eight unworked mixed questions, explicitly described as an inventory rather than a mandatory workload. The Biology pack gives the percentage-change formula, guidance to distinguish an observed rate trend from its mechanism, and guidance to preserve enzyme amount, substrate, pH, timing and measurement method while changing the intended independent variable. The planner may author additional self-contained examples and independent checks if givens, answers or feedback, and stopping criteria are clear. A calculator is allowed. No paid website or undisclosed textbook is needed.
summary.strengths: The diagnostic evidence shows that Amina correctly balanced three simpler chemical equations without help and correctly described diffusion down a concentration gradient. She also reports recognising worked examples, although that recognition is not itself evidence of independent transfer.
summary.background: Amina is an upper-secondary student. English is a comfortable second language. School has covered the topics once. She has no private tutor and no paid question bank. Her available tools are a phone, paper, calculator and the three supplied teacher packets: a school mock scope notice, her diagnostic answers with teacher annotations, and a teacher practice pack. The documents present school mock assessments, not an external exam-board specification.
summary.weaknesses: Her self-reported confidence in moles conflicts with the diagnostic performance. In Chemistry she multiplied 12 g by 24 g/mol to obtain 288 mol, failed to convert 250 mL to litres and wrote 50 mol, and treated hydrogen as limiting because its coefficient was larger. In Biology she recorded a fall from 20.0 g to 18.0 g as +10% and said water moved into the tissue, said active transport needs no energy, changed both temperature and enzyme concentration in an enzyme investigation, and concluded that every decrease in rate proved denaturation. Teacher annotations identify chemical arithmetic, unit conversion, limiting-reagent reasoning, osmosis direction, controlled variables and overclaiming from data as needing work. Her report that she often recognises worked examples but gets stuck when numbers or wording change is consistent with the diagnostic, but transfer to unfamiliar contexts remains unverified.
summary.constraints: The Chemistry deadline is fixed at 19 November 2026 and the Biology deadline at 22 November 2026, three days later. Exam-day study is not allowed. Friday must remain free. The existing English reading submission is a 35-minute commitment on 1 November 2026. Only the uploaded packets are authorised; no web browsing or resource purchase is permitted. The confirmed capacity envelope, rest days and excluded dates bound available time, and if full useful work does not fit, the conflict must be explained rather than deleting education or increasing availability.
summary.preferences: Amina prefers sessions of about 35–50 minutes and wants to avoid fragmented five-minute checklist tasks. She wants an explanation of why a method applies before attempting work independently. She prefers useful explanation and independent application over rereading or arbitrary question counts, wants Friday kept free, and does not want spare time filled with unnecessary work.
summary.uncertainty: The uploaded documents are private teacher/student materials whose issuer authority was not independently established. Their content can support the school project's stated scope and resources, but it cannot be treated as an external exam-board specification or official board statement. There is no accepted execution history and no post-diagnostic independent performance evidence, so general mastery and transfer to unfamiliar numbers or wording are unverified. The three hours of video watching is self-report and supplies no performance credit. Exact official weighting of explanation, calculation and unfamiliar-data questions is not stated.

sections.text: These are school mock assessments, not an external exam-board specification. Chemistry is 21 days after the frozen study anchor, biology 24 days after it; both begin at 09:00 local time. Exam-day study is not available. Chemistry: amount of substance, molar mass, solution concentration, balancing equations, reacting amounts, limiting reagents. Biology: diffusion, osmosis, active transport, interpreting mass changes and rates, enzyme conditions, controls and conclusions. Each paper mixes explanation, calculation and unfamiliar-data questions. No other chapters are assessed. Students may use a calculator. The teacher expects method justification and units, not memorized worked answers. The student has already supplied the school and exact scope; do not ask which external exam board applies.

result.text: {"action":"COMPLETE","summary":{"goals":"Amina is preparing for two fixed school mock assessments: Chemistry first, with the outcome of independently solving and explaining amount-of-substance, concentration, balanced-equation and limiting-reagent problems, including unfamiliar numbers and error checks; and Biology three days later, with the outcome of explaining cell transport and enzyme investigations, interpreting unfamiliar data and justifying an independent experimental conclusion. She also wants to preserve both outcomes, keep Friday free and retain the existing English reading submission. She prefers useful explanation and independent application over rereading or arbitrary question counts.","background":"Amina is an upper-secondary student. English is a comfortable second language. School has covered the topics once. She has no private tutor and no paid question bank. Her available tools are a phone, paper, calculator and the three supplied teacher packets: a school mock scope notice, her diagnostic answers with teacher annotations, and a teacher practice pack. The documents present school mock assessments, not an external exam-board specification.","strengths":"The diagnostic evidence shows that Amina correctly balanced three simpler chemical equations without help and correctly described diffusion down a concentration gradient. She also reports recognising worked examples, although that recognition is not itself evidence of independent transfer.","weaknesses":"Her self-reported confidence in moles conflicts with the diagnostic performance. In Chemistry she multiplied 12 g by 24 g/mol to obtain 288 mol, failed to convert 250 mL to litres and wrote 50 mol, and treated hydrogen as limiting because its coefficient was larger. In Biology she recorded a fall from 20.0 g to 18.0 g as +10% and said water moved into the tissue, said active transport needs no energy, changed both temperature and enzyme concentration in an enzyme investigation, and concluded that every decrease in rate proved denaturation. Teacher annotations identify chemical arithmetic, unit conversion, limiting-reagent reasoning, osmosis direction, controlled variables and overclaiming from data as needing work. Her report that she often recognises worked examples but gets stuck when numbers or wording change is consistent with the diagnostic, but transfer to unfamiliar contexts remains unverified.","resources":"Three uploaded teacher/student documents are available. The Chemistry pack includes worked examples showing division of grams by grams per mole, conversion of millilitres to litres, and comparison of supplied amount divided by coefficient before using the smaller reaction extent. It also contains eight unworked mixed questions, explicitly described as an inventory rather than a mandatory workload. The Biology pack gives the percentage-change formula, guidance to distinguish an observed rate trend from its mechanism, and guidance to preserve enzyme amount, substrate, pH, timing and measurement method while changing the intended independent variable. The planner may author additional self-contained examples and independent checks if givens, answers or feedback, and stopping criteria are clear. A calculator is allowed. No paid website or undisclosed textbook is needed.","constraints":"The Chemistry deadline is fixed at 19 November 2026 and the Biology deadline at 22 November 2026, three days later. Exam-day study is not allowed. Friday must remain free. The existing English reading submission is a 35-minute commitment on 1 November 2026. Only the uploaded packets are authorised; no web browsing or resource purchase is permitted. The confirmed capacity envelope, rest days and excluded dates bound available time, and if full useful work does not fit, the conflict must be explained rather than deleting education or increasing availability.","preferences":"Amina prefers sessions of about 35–50 minutes and wants to avoid fragmented five-minute checklist tasks. She wants an explanation of why a method applies before attempting work independently.
